clue.text: Dollars stolen to get hunter's requisite

parts.note: bucks is slang for dollars
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A thief pockets cash to buy what a hunter needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead pellets fired from a shotgun are standard ammunition for anyone out shooting game.

clue.text: Container suitable for male alien

parts.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: Someone picks a receptacle that would suit a visiting man from space.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is an open vessel for carrying water, so it is a kind of receptacle.

clue.text: See Pam change drastically given drink

indicators.note: changing something drastically rearranges it completely, so the letters of these two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Watch Pam undergo a dramatic transformation after being handed a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drastically' tells you to rearrange PAM and CHANGE; 'See' and 'given' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparkling wine from France's Champagne region is a celebratory beverage.

clue.text: Italian gentlemen authorise gold to be given to one

parts.note: to sign something is to authorise it
or is gold in heraldry
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Italian men approve a gift of gold to a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: Signori is the Italian plural for men addressed politely, the equivalent of sirs or misters.

clue.text: Curiously dry old cracks, short of water, ultimately

indicators.note: something that cracks breaks up, so the letters of the two words are broken and rearranged
the last letter of the word water is R, and being short of it removes that R from dry

explanation.surface: Strangely, parched old ground splits open for lack of water.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop R (the last letter of 'water') from DRY to leave DY, then 'cracks' shuffles DY with OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs meaning in a strange or peculiar way.

clue.text: Peeled plum swallowed by writer's dog

indicators.note: being swallowed means going inside, so the peeled fruit sits within the writer

parts.note: Saki was the pen name of the short-story writer H. H. Munro

indicators.note: a peeled fruit loses its skin, so the outer letters of plum go, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A dog belonging to an author gulps down a skinned plum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peeled' strips plum to LU, which goes inside SAKI.
explanation.definitionFit: The saluki is a slender Middle Eastern hunting hound, a breed of canine.

clue.text: Add tape freshly, having made change

indicators.note: doing something freshly makes it anew, so the letters of these two words are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone applies new sticky tape after altering something.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to alter or modify, so the past participle describes something that has been altered.

clue.text: Remove ropes from a French oil platform

parts.note: un is the French for a
a rig is an offshore oil-drilling platform

explanation.surface: Strip the rigging off a French offshore drilling structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigging is a ship's system of ropes, so to take the rigging off is to strip away its lines.

clue.text: Silliness about saint is madness

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the silliness word wraps round the saint

parts.note: inanity is silliness or pointlessness

explanation.surface: Foolishness surrounding a holy figure is called lunacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name mental derangement or wild folly.

clue.text: Naturally relating to golf?

explanation.surface: Of course golf is natural, says the enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally is an adverb meaning certainly, as expected; read literally, the phrase means concerning the links where golf is played.

clue.text: Cost for unfaithfulness of diplomat?

parts.note: read as a fee levied on an envoy's extramarital dalliances: the first word of the title means charged, the second sounds like love affairs

explanation.surface: What price does an ambassador pay for cheating on a spouse?
explanation.walkthrough: The title of a deputy envoy splits into CHARGED (cost) and AFFAIRES, which looks like affairs, the infidelities.
explanation.definitionFit: This French title names a diplomat who heads a mission in the ambassador's absence.

clue.text: Union? False

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Union? False (7)', gives only EU + PHONY wordplay; no word defines a pleasing sound, so the definition is missing from the printed text.

clue.text: Figure a month's past before 1st of November

indicators.note: before places the month and past ahead of the letter from November

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October, a month
ago means in the past

indicators.note: 1st of takes just the opening letter of the following word, November

explanation.surface: A calendar figure: a month gone by, just before the start of November.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-sided polygon is a geometrical shape.

clue.text: Shining silver on scattered rubbish

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
litter is waste strewn about

explanation.surface: Bright silver lies on strewn rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the definition of LITTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean sparkling or glittering brightly.

clue.text: Awful dog without tail brings in empty bowl

indicators.note: bringing in means taking inside, so the shortened dog contains the emptied bowl
losing the tail drops the last letter of the dog breed

parts.note: a terrier is a breed of dog

indicators.note: an empty word loses its insides, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dreadful dog with no tail carries in a bowl with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: TERRIER loses its last letter to give TERRIE; 'empty' leaves BL from bowl, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean extremely bad or dreadful.

clue.text: Understand Information Technology character?

parts.note: dig is slang for understand or appreciate

explanation.surface: Do you grasp what a computing personality is like?
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral such as 7 is one of the symbols used in writing, a typographic character.

clue.text: Hamlet in which you'd find canine?

definitions.text: Hamlet in which you'd find canine?

parts.words: Hamlet in which you'd find canine?
parts.note: Hamlet is a celebrated prince of Denmark, and a large dog breed carries the same description

explanation.surface: Which village is home to a dog?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' looks like a small village, but it is Shakespeare's prince, a famous man of Denmark; the same title names a giant dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant dog breed and Shakespeare's prince are both a celebrated Dane.

clue.text: West's kind about conductors

parts.note: Mae West was the American film star; with the 's it gives her name plus S

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for kind is read backwards

parts.note: sort means kind or type

explanation.surface: An actor's type of person surrounds orchestra leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: Mae West was a Hollywood actress; 'about' turns SORT into TROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestro is a title for a distinguished orchestral leader, so the plural names those who lead orchestras.

clue.text: Drink at right time makes one wide awake

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A beer at the proper moment keeps one fully alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions describe being fully attentive and watchful.

clue.text: Acid permitted in small pastry

parts.note: tart means sharp or sour, like acid
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A sour flavour is allowed in a little baked treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartlet is a little pie or flan, a diminutive tart.

clue.text: Right tone set by information on unit of radiation

indicators.note: set here means arranged or put in order, so the letters of tone are rearranged

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Correct the tone using data about measuring radiation.
explanation.definitionFit: The roentgen is an old measure of exposure to X-rays and gamma rays.

clue.text: Continue to tease in English town

parts.note: taunt means tease or mock
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: Keep on mocking people in a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: TAUNTON is the county town of Somerset in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Taunton is a town in Somerset, England.

clue.text: Novel hat

explanation.surface: A new type of headwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the noun: Trilby is an 1894 novel by George du Maurier.
explanation.definitionFit: The book by du Maurier gave its title to a soft felt hat with a narrow brim, worn in its stage version.

clue.text: Warriors, fighting Masai, besieging old city

indicators.note: besieging surrounds a place, so the shuffled tribe name encloses the old city
fighting suggests a scuffle that jumbles the letters of Masai

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Masai warriors in combat lay siege to an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighting' rearranges MASAI into SAMAI, which goes round UR.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the hereditary military class of feudal Japan, sword-bearing fighters.

clue.text: Unusual bay in Maine? It's not certain

indicators.note: in places the rearranged bay inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

indicators.note: unusual signals an odd arrangement of the letters of bay

explanation.surface: Is there a strange bay in Maine? Nobody is sure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges BAY into AYB, inside ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps is a hedging word used when something is uncertain.

clue.text: Disturb fellow, lecherous type

parts.note: a luster is one who lusts, a lecherous person

explanation.surface: A man is unsettled by a lustful character.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluster is to agitate or confuse someone, to upset their composure.

clue.text: Father, always comparatively liberal

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A priest is forever more open-minded than others.
explanation.definitionFit: Free can mean liberal or unrestrained, so the comparative form means more liberal.

clue.text: Far from common concert venue?

parts.note: far from common suggests aristocratic, regal, and the clue asks for a grand music hall that sounds anything but ordinary

explanation.surface: Where can one hear music somewhere that is decidedly upmarket?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far from common' is read as royal, the opposite of a commoner; the London concert hall named after Queen Victoria's consort fits.
explanation.definitionFit: This domed auditorium in Kensington, London, hosts concerts including the Proms.

clue.text: Cold and wet? Shelter in beastly place

indicators.note: in places the shelter inside the animal's home

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs, a place for beasts
lee is shelter from the wind

explanation.surface: Is it chilly and damp in a shelter within a nasty spot?
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' looks like an insult, but a beastly place is a home for beasts, a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather with half-frozen rain falling is chilly and damp.

clue.text: House by railway where fruit is grown

parts.note: the House of Orange is the Dutch royal dynasty

explanation.surface: A house next to a railway line where fruit trees are raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' here is a royal dynasty, the House of Orange, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: This glass building was originally used to grow citrus trees in cold climates.
